;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2015–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Houthis|Houthi forces]] capture the city of [[Al Hazm, Yemen|Al Hazm]], the capital of [[Al Jawf Governorate]] in [[Yemen]]. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20200302-yemen-houthis-seize-strategic-city-bordering-saudi-arabia/ (Middle East Monitor)] [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/03/officials-yemen-rebels-seize-strategic-northern-city-200301135153794.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Syrian Civil War]], [[Northwestern Syria offensive (December 2019–March 2020)]]
**[[Syrian rebels]] backed by [[Turkey]] recapture four towns and villages from the [[Syrian government]] forces in [[Idlib Governorate|Idlib]], raising the number of towns and villages recaptured since February 24 to 30. [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=366544 (SOHR)]
**Syrian government forces backed by [[Russian Air Force|Russian]] [[airstrike]]s recapture the city of [[Saraqib]] four days after its capture by the rebels. [http://www.syriahr.com/?p=366546 (SOHR)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]], [[Afghan peace process]]
**The [[Taliban]] say there will be no intra-Afghan talks if about 5,000 of their prisoners are not released. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan-taliban-idUSKBN20P1FZ (Reuters)]
**The Taliban announce the end of the period of reduction in violence. They say they will not attack [[Resolute Support Mission|foreign]] troops, but continue their operations against [[Cabinet of Afghanistan|Kabul government]] troops. According to [[Belga (news agency)|Belga]] news agency, it is unclear what the announcement means for the [[Afghan peace process#2020 agreement|U.S.–Taliban agreement]] signed on February 29. [https://www.hln.be/nieuws/buitenland/taliban-breekt-wapenstilstand-amper-twee-dagen-na-akkoord-met-vs~a152f64b/ (Belga via ''Het Laatste Nieuws'')]
*[[European migrant crisis]]
**[[Hellenic Police]] [[border guard]]s open fire on [[immigration to Greece|migrants]] attempting to [[illegal immigration|illegally]] enter [[Greece]] by crossing the [[Greece–Turkey border|border]] from [[Turkey]], killing a [[Syrians|Syrian]] man. [https://www.france24.com/en/20200302-syrian-migrant-killed-as-thousands-attempt-to-cross-from-turkey-into-greece (France 24)] [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20200302-syrian-refugee-trying-to-cross-border-killed-by-greek-police/ (Middle East Monitor)]
**The [[Hellenic Army]]'s [[IV Army Corps (Greece)|IV Army Corps]] announces a 24-hour snap [[Military exercise|military drill]] on the border with Turkey, and warns civilians to stay away from the area. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/greece-to-conduct-military-exercise-near-turkish-border/1751914 (Anadolu Angency)]
*[[Moro conflict]]
**A [[Philippine Army|soldier]] was killed and two injured after [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]-linked militants opened fire against them. Two [[terrorism in the Philippines|terrorist]]s were also killed. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2020-03/03/c_138838597.htm (Xinhua)]

;Business and economy
*[[Economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic]]
**The [[Japan Sumo Association]] announces its spring tournament in [[Osaka]] will take place [[Behind closed doors (sport)|with no spectators]]. [http://www.newsonjapan.com/html/newsdesk/article/126478.php (News On Japan)]
**The [[Dow Jones Industrial Average]] rebounds 1,294 points to end its seven day decline. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/03/02/investing/dow-stock-market-today/index.html (CNN)]

**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington (state)]]
****Two dozen more cases are reported in the U.S., bringing the total number of infected Americans to 102. Four deaths also occur in the state of [[Washington (state)|Washington]], bringing the total death toll in the U.S. to six. Washington and [[Florida]] issue state emergencies. [https://www.cnn.com/2020/03/02/health/us-coronavirus-cases-monday/index.html (CNN)]

***[[Ecuador]] reports its first cases in [[Guayaquil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-china-health-ecuador/ecuador-confirms-five-new-cases-of-coronavirus-all-close-to-initial-patient-idUSKBN20O2EE (Reuters)]

;International relations
*The [[United Kingdom]] and the [[European Union]] start [[Continuing United Kingdom relationship with the European Union|post-Brexit]] trade talks. Last week, each side publicly set its negotiating mandate. [https://www.economist.com/britain/2020/03/01/the-eu-and-britain-start-negotiating-a-post-brexit-trade-deal (''The Economist'')] [https://www.irishtimes.com/news/politics/uk-breaching-brexit-deal-would-be-big-break-of-trust-former-wto-head-1.4189495 (''The Irish Times'')]
*[[Japan–North Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea]] fires two short-range projectiles from the coast of [[Wonsan]] before landing in the sea dividing the [[Korea|Korean Peninsula]] and [[Japan]]. Japan's Defence Ministry says it had not detected any projectile landing in its territory and that no ship or aircraft in the area had been damaged. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/02/north-korea-fires-two-projectiles-ending-its-ban-on-long-range-tests (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Libyan peace process]]
**The head of the [[United Nations Support Mission in Libya]] [[Ghassan Salamé]] resigns citing stress and health concerns. In a statement on [[Twitter]], Salamé says he has been frustrated with foreign powers, particularly [[France]] and [[Russia]] for covertly backing [[Khalifa Haftar]]'s forces in the [[Libyan Civil War (2014–present)|civil war]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/mar/02/libya-peace-efforts-chaos-un-envoy-ghassan-salam-quits (''The Guardian'')]

;Law and crime
*A [[hostage]] situation occurs at the [[Greenhills (mall)|V-Mall]] in [[San Juan, Metro Manila|San Juan]], [[Philippines]]. The suspect, a disgruntled security guard, took about 60 to 70 people hostage and shot and injured another security guard. The crisis is resolved after ten hours, with the suspect being arrested following an official apology and the resignation of his bosses for alleged corruption. [https://cnnphilippines.com/news/2020/3/2/V-Mall-Virra-Mall-Greenhills-shooting-incident.html (CNN Philippines)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Dominican Republic municipal elections]]
**Industrial Associations Federation's president Ramón Porfirio Báez announces the election crisis is beginning to hurt the economy. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/economy/2020/03/02/botched-elections-harms-the-economy-all-sectors/ (''Dominican Today'')]
**Former [[Santo Domingo]] mayor [[Roberto Salcedo Sr.]] resigns from the government and the [[Dominican Liberation Party]]. [https://dominicantoday.com/dr/local/2020/03/02/high-level-figure-quits-the-ruling-party-could-herald-stampede/ (''Dominican Today'')]  
*[[2020 Guyanese general election]]
**People of [[Guyana]] head to the polls to elect the members of their [[National Assembly (Guyana)|National Assembly]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/02/guyana-holds-crucial-election-expected-oil-boom-200228214328135.html (AlJazeera)]
*[[2020 Israeli legislative election]]
**[[Israel]]is head to the polls for the third time in less than a year. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-israel-election/mired-in-stalemate-israel-holds-another-election-on-netanyahus-future-idUSKBN20P00F (Reuters)]
*[[2020 Democratic Party presidential primaries]]
**[[Minnesota]] [[United States Senate|Senator]] [[Amy Klobuchar]] suspends her [[Amy Klobuchar 2020 presidential campaign|presidential campaign]], and joins fellow former contenders [[Pete Buttigieg]] and [[Beto O'Rourke]] in [[List of Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign endorsements|announcing their endorsement]] of [[Joe Biden]]. [https://www.nytimes.com./2020/03/02/us/politics/amy-klobuchar-drops-out.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[MSNBC]] political anchor [[Chris Matthews]] resigns over criticism of making sexist comments and comparing [[Bernie Sanders]]' campaign to the [[German military administration in occupied France during World War II|Nazi invasion of France]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2020/03/02/business/media/chris-matthews-resigns-steps-down-msnbc.html (''The New York Times'')]
